comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C5 regarding reconstruction completeness and quantitative data. Both evaluations find the data supported, with OpenEval emphasizing methodological transparency and peer reviewers praising the 'painstakingly meticulous' and 'exceptional, high-quality' work.

Perfect agreement on claims C6-C12 regarding gross anatomical organization. Both evaluations support these structural descriptions as part of the high-quality dataset, with no concerns raised about the neuroanatomical characterization.

Strong agreement on morphological claims C13-C19, though peer review R3 also encompasses C20-C24 from OpenEval R4. Both find the quantitative morphological data and correlations well-supported as part of the comprehensive 'wealth of data.'

Agreement on ultrastructural features C20-C24. Peer review groups these morphological characterizations (C13-C24) together as part of the meticulous analysis, while OpenEval separates quantitative measurements (R3) from ultrastructural descriptions (R4).

Perfect agreement on network-level statistics C25-C30. Both evaluations support the graph analyses and connectivity patterns, with peer reviewers noting the work provides detailed information about how different neuron types are connected.

Perfect agreement on module identification C31-C37. Both evaluations support the Leiden algorithm approach and functional validation through citations, with peer reviewers specifically noting the value for studies on modules and cell type diversity.

Perfect agreement on cell-type classification C38-C44. Both evaluations find the comprehensive classification well-supported, with peer reviewers emphasizing this work 'lays the foundations for studies on cell type diversity.'

Perfect agreement on grouped connectome C45-C48. Both evaluations support the bilateral symmetry findings and comparative analysis, with peer reviewers noting this is 'only the third whole body connectome to be assembled.'

Perfect agreement on circuit depth analysis C49-C53. Both evaluations support the path-finding analyses and identification of neurosecretory cells, accepting these as part of the high-quality connectivity analysis.

Perfect agreement on molecular integration C54-C57. Both evaluations support the neuropeptide assignments and ultrastructural correlations, with peer reviewers accepting the molecular characterization as part of the comprehensive dataset despite noting the paper is 'burdensome to read.'

Agreement on head circuit organization C58-C60, though peer review R10 encompasses broader head circuit claims (C58-C70). Both evaluations support the connectivity patterns and recurrent connectivity findings as part of the detailed circuit-level analysis.

Agreement on motor circuits C61-C66. Peer review R10 groups these with other head circuits (C58-C70), while OpenEval separates specific motor circuits. Both find the anatomical descriptions and functional inferences appropriately supported.

Agreement on integrative neurons C67-C70. Peer review R10 includes these claims within broader head circuit analysis (C58-C70), while OpenEval treats them separately. Both support the network centrality measures and convergence patterns.

Strong agreement on mushroom body anatomy C71-C78. Both evaluations support the detailed MB characterization, with peer reviewers specifically noting this 'lays the foundations for studies on mushroom bodies' and suggesting the depth could warrant a separate paper.

Notable difference in evaluation type for MB circuit function C79-C81. OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature of C81, while peer reviewers mark as SUPPORTED. Both acknowledge the hypothesis is appropriately tentative, but peer reviewers accept it as part of 'several interesting conclusions.'

Perfect agreement on head-trunk connectivity C82-C86. Both evaluations support the quantification and anatomical descriptions of descending/ascending pathways as part of the analysis of 'long-range and short-range connectivity.'

Perfect agreement on segmental organization C87-C96. Both evaluations strongly support this analysis, with peer reviewers noting it 'lays the foundations for studies on segmental vs. intersegmental connectivity' and 'informs the understanding of the evolution of segmental body plans.'

Strong agreement on segment-specific cell types C97-C104, with peer review R14 also including C105. Both evaluations support the heteromeric organization and novel findings like pygidial pigment-motor neurons as part of comprehensive segment characterization.

Agreement on serial homology C105-C107, though peer review R15 focuses on C106-C107. Both evaluations support the evolutionary inference as appropriately tentative, with peer reviewers noting conclusions about 'circuit evolution by duplication and diversion of cell types.'

Partial overlap on C105 between OpenEval R19 and peer R14. OpenEval groups C105 with evolutionary interpretation (C106-C107), while peer review includes it with segment-specific cell types (C97-C105), reflecting different organizational perspectives on the same data.

Perfect agreement on mechanosensory girdle C108-C112. Both evaluations support this novel anatomical system identification, with peer reviewers accepting it as part of the detailed circuit analysis revealing body-wide organizational principles.

Agreement on chaeMech neurons C113-C119, though peer review R17 encompasses broader mechanosensory analysis (C113-C126). Both evaluations support the anatomical characterization and comparative analysis, accepting functional speculation as appropriately tentative.

Agreement on mechanosensory convergence C120-C126. Peer review R17 groups these with chaeMech characterization (C113-C126), while OpenEval separates them. Both support the connectivity patterns and functional hypotheses about proprioceptive feedback.

Perfect agreement on INsplit interneuron family C127-C135. Both evaluations strongly support the comprehensive characterization, cell-type-specific connectivity patterns, and conclusions about mechanosensory input reaching all effector systems.
